Reflection: the final structure is now clear and both directions of the mechanism are strong. On the long side, replacing the static leverage channel with the *debt-issuance flow* channel gave the best risk-adjusted result (RealGrowthWithDebtIssuanceQuality: FMB 3.95, alpha +5.6%, t=4.02, Sharpe 0.599), and the four-channel version confirmed both debt measures carry information (alpha 5.8%, Sharpe 0.583). On the short side, debt-funded expansion conditioned on the full three-channel quality score is the archive's most reliable signal of all (alpha −6.3%, t=−4.17, Sharpe −0.584). Two clear negatives close off directions: cash-flow volatility as a quality channel damaged the signal badly (FMB 3.68→2.05, Sharpe 0.534→0.280), and lengthening the growth window to two years cost both alpha and coverage. Centering the quality score (ZSCORE) was neutral on alpha, so it is worth one final test against the better channel set. This last batch therefore unifies the long and short constructions into a single financing-quality-of-expansion signal (signals 1 and 6, my recommended final candidates), pushes the short side once more, and tests two remaining quality channels — short-term liquidity and total obligations — that the composite has never contained.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: DebtFreeRealExpansionWithCashQuality
EXPRESSION: MUL(SUMRANK(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(at, che), 1), LAG(at, 1)), NEG(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), LAG(at, 1)))), SUMRANK(MA(RATIO(SUB(oancf, capx), at), 3), NEG(MA(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 3))))
HYPOTHESIS: The single most informative expansion measure is real operating-asset growth achieved without new borrowing; combined with persistent free cash flow and cash-backed earnings, it identifies firms whose capacity growth is genuinely self-financed rather than levered up.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This unifies the two best archive results, which are mirror images of one another: the long side rewards ex-cash asset growth conditioned on cash quality (alpha +5.6% to +5.9%) while the short side punishes debt-financed expansion conditioned on the same quality (alpha −6.3%); putting debt issuance into the *investment* leg with a negative sign rather than into the quality leg makes the economic statement directly — expansion is good only when it is not borrowed. Keeping the quality leg to the two cash-flow channels avoids double-counting debt information now that leverage is expressed in the investment leg. This is my primary candidate for the final signal.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: CenteredCashQualityTimesRealGrowth
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(at, che), 1), LAG(at, 1))), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(MA(RATIO(SUB(oancf, capx), at), 3), SUMRANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 3)), NEG(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), LAG(at, 1)))))))
HYPOTHESIS: Because the theme's claim is a sign flip, the interaction should multiply expansion by a cross-sectionally centered quality score so that growth is rewarded above the quality median and penalized below it, producing a spread that is long high-growth/high-quality and short high-growth/low-quality firms.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Centering was neutral for alpha when tested with the leverage-level channel set (5.9%, Sharpe 0.533), but the debt-issuance channel set has since proven superior on every metric, so the combination has not been evaluated and is the natural last functional-form test. If it lifts the Sharpe above 0.599 while holding alpha near 5.6%, the centered form is the cleaner final specification because both portfolio legs are matched on investment intensity and cannot be a disguised profitability sort. It changes only the centering of the conditioner relative to the current leader.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: LeveredExpansionByLowQualityFirms
EXPRESSION: MUL(SUMRANK(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), LAG(at, 1)), RATIO(DELTA(SUB(at, che), 1), LAG(at, 1))), NEG(SUMRANK(MA(RATIO(SUB(oancf, capx), at), 3), SUMRANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 3)), NEG(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at))))))
HYPOTHESIS: The most value-destroying configuration is a large real expansion that is simultaneously debt-funded, undertaken by a firm with cash-flow deficits, heavy accruals and an already-levered balance sheet; requiring both the borrowing and the asset build in the investment leg should identify it more sharply than borrowing alone.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The current best short conditions only on debt growth (alpha −6.3%, t=−4.17), which includes firms that borrow to refinance or to hold cash rather than to expand; adding ex-cash asset growth to the investment leg via SUMRANK restricts the short leg to genuine levered expanders. This is the one remaining sharpening of the archive's most statistically reliable signal, and it keeps the same conditioner so the comparison is clean. A deeper negative alpha would establish a matched long/short pair from one mechanism.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: BorrowedGrowthWithWeakDebtCoverage
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), LAG(at, 1))), NEG(SUMRANK(MA(RATIO(SUB(oancf, capx), at), 3), SUMRANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 3)), RATIO(MA(oancf, 3), ADD(dltt, dlc))))))
HYPOTHESIS: What makes new borrowing dangerous is the inability to service it: cash-flow-to-debt coverage, a flow-over-stock measure, should condition the debt-funded expansion penalty more precisely than the leverage ratio, which ignores how much cash the existing debt load actually consumes.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Debt-service coverage showed a genuine standalone effect earlier (alpha +3.4%, t=2.47) but was never combined with the debt-growth investment leg that now drives the archive's best short-side evidence, so this substitutes coverage for the leverage level while holding everything else fixed. It is the informative solvency ablation on the short side, mirroring the leverage-versus-issuance ablation that improved the long side in generation 8. Both variables are already in use, so coverage is unaffected.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: RealGrowthWithLiquidityBuffer
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(at, che), 1), LAG(at, 1))), SUMRANK(MA(RATIO(SUB(oancf, capx), at), 3), SUMRANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 3)), RATIO(act, lct))))
HYPOTHESIS: Fragility during an expansion is partly a working-capital phenomenon: firms whose current assets comfortably cover current liabilities can absorb the working-capital drain that accompanies growth, while illiquid expanders are forced into distress financing or fire sales.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Short-term liquidity is the one classic quality dimension never included in the winning composite — the archive has tested cash flow levels, accruals, leverage, debt issuance, coverage, volatility and lifecycle, but not the current ratio — and it captures near-term financing stress rather than long-horizon solvency. Because the failed volatility test showed that not every plausible channel adds value, this is a genuine test rather than a template variation, and both inputs are near-universally reported so coverage is preserved. If it improves on the leader, near-term liquidity is the operative fragility margin.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: SelfFinancedExpansionFullQuality
EXPRESSION: MUL(SUMRANK(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(at, che), 1), LAG(at, 1)), NEG(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), LAG(at, 1)))), SUMRANK(MA(RATIO(SUB(oancf, capx), at), 3), SUMRANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 3)), NEG(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Productive investment is real operating-asset expansion funded from internal cash rather than new debt, undertaken by firms with cash-backed earnings and spare balance-sheet capacity; all four pieces of evidence — expansion, no new borrowing, cash conversion, low leverage — should reinforce one another.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This is signal 1 plus the leverage-level channel, and the pair identifies whether the pre-existing debt stock still matters once new borrowing has been moved into the investment leg — the last unresolved design question in the winning family, given that both debt measures added value when both sat in the quality leg. Every component has been individually validated in this archive, and the ranked aggregation keeps any single accounting item from dominating. Together with signal 1 it gives the final generation two closely matched candidates whose comparison determines the most parsimonious specification.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
